extracted.intended_audience: judges, in-house counsel, and outside patent litigators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and best practices for courts, plaintiffs, and defendants to manage patent litigation efficiently — keeping cases from overrunning court dockets, controlling discovery, and managing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective use of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage available resources early and deliberately to manage workload and expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include engaging external experts and consultants early, utilizing technology for case management, and considering early dispositive motions or creative discovery schedules to focus efforts and reduce unnecessary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline the discovery process
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a detailed substantive assessment of risks and tailor discovery to what is necessary rather than permit broad, fishing expeditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement focused discovery (not fishing); provide initial document disclosures on conception of the invention, operation of the accused product, and damages; streamline the scope of discovery to core areas (patent claims, relevant prior art, invalidity grounds, specific discovery requests, and 30(b)(6) topics); rely on summary judgment where appropriate; follow existing guidance (Sedona Conference, Federal Circuit Advisory Council) to limit disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiate and compromise to avoid costly disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize negotiation and reasonable compromise when discovery or pre-trial disputes arise to prevent expensive, protracted fights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensively negotiate discovery and pre-trial disputes; recognize that compromise is acceptable to reduce costs and conserve judicial resources. The panel emphasizes working to avoid discovery disputes because they are cost-intensive and frustrate the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus claim construction on disputes that matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit claim construction disputes to terms and issues that have a legitimate chance of affecting the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess which claim construction disputes are central to liability or damages and concentrate resources on those; avoid expansive claim-construction battles over peripheral terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost management and budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt measures to control litigation spend and align expenditures with case value and business priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement creative case schedules to concentrate on damages or key liability issues, use efficient legal research and document management, adopt simple ESI protocols and an e-discovery liaison, know your litigation and settlement bottom lines early, and explore design-around options while considering how they will be presented at trial. Use AIPLA and other survey data to inform budgeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative proceedings (e.g., IPR) to reduce cost/exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate inter partes review and other alternatives as potentially lower-cost avenues to resolve patent validity/exposure issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR can be a fraction of litigation cost (noted range $350k–$600k through trial per AIPLA Survey 2023). Weigh benefits/costs of IPR versus district-court litigation, and consider impacts (e.g., jury reaction to design-arounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the client’s business and align litigation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure litigation planning reflects the client’s commercial goals, risk tolerance, and business context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align the litigation plan with business goals to better assess potential risks and outcomes and to set litigation priorities that make sense for the client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive preparation and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare early and set clear priorities to position the case effectively and prevent reactive, costly litigation conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro-active planning should establish what matters most for the case early (e.g., liability drivers, key evidence, damages issues) so teams can focus resources appropriately and reduce wasted effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage technology and efficient processes for document/ESI management
rubrics_metrics.description: Use technology and streamlined processes to reduce time and expense in managing documents and ESI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt case-management technology, efficient document-management workflows, simple ESI protocols, and designate an e-discovery liaison to coordinate discovery and limit duplication of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial case-management to reduce docket time
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts should employ tools and procedures that constrain runaway cases and shorten the time cases remain on the docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges can regain control through active docket management, encouraging narrow discovery, insisting on focused disputes, and utilizing scheduling and dispositive motion practices that limit protracted discovery fights which often cost more than the rest of a case combined.
